pages.visible_text: Record type 72-hour reconstruction Observed, not forecast Observed period 2026-10-25 to 2026-10-27 Integrity Complete Required observation coverage passed Updated 2026-10-28 17:17 UTC Debrecen, Hungary - 2026-10-25 to 2026-10-27 Methods And Data Transparent baselines, explainable regime rules, source notes, and downloadable outputs for the current report. Climatological Reference Ledger Metric This period 1991-2020 mean (anomaly) Recent 10-year mean (anomaly) 1990-present percentile Temperature 9.2 9.7 (-0.5) 11.5 (-2.3) 44th Precipitation 8.5 3.3 (+5.2) 6.3 (+2.2) 83th Wind 6.1 5.0 (+1.1) 5.2 (+0.9) 69th Pressure 1018.1 1019.6 (-1.5) 1017.6 (+0.5) 36th Cloud 59.8 55.0 (+4.8) 52.9 (+6.9) 53th Solar radiation 5605.0 6187.3 (-582.3) 6091.7 (-486.7) 39th Classification Signals no single signal dominated mixed day-to-day conditions Sources And Quality HungaroMet supplies Debrecen Airport observations, composite radar, LINET lightning and Meteosat imagery. Open-Meteo supplies the continuous gridded surface record, pressure-level model fields, synoptic grid, the wide-domain 850 hPa wind field the back-trajectory integrates through, land fields and ERA5 climate archive. Standard normals use 1991-2020; the recent comparison retains the prior 10 years and is stored in baseline_metrics.csv. Data completeness check passed with 73/73 expected local-period hours. The radar archive retains about 71 hours, so the oldest 41 frame(s) of this 146-frame window are structurally unavailable rather than missing. Radar coverage 53/105 (50%) of the reachable window is below the 90% threshold. The radar input did not meet its completeness threshold and is reported as incomplete rather than presented as whole. Hungary-wide electricity context from Energy-Charts (primarily ENTSO-E data). Model-derived atmospheric profile near Debrecen; it is not an observed radiosonde. Dew point is calculated from model temperature and relative humidity. HungaroMet station 64711 (Debrecen Airport); 10-minute observations. Station coverage: 438/438 expected records (100%). HungaroMet 1 km composite radar sampled every 30 minutes; 107/146 frames available (73%). The browser replay uses every 60 minutes and a 3 km display grid for practical loading. Accumulation is a reflectivity-derived Z-R estimate and should be treated as a spatial precipitation proxy. HungaroMet LINET events within 150 km of Debrecen. Detected 5 lightning events in the reporting period. HungaroMet Meteosat Second Generation RGB and infrared products; frames sampled approximately every 180 minutes. Satellite imagery is synchronized by nearest timestamp with radar and LINET timelines, not spatially overlaid. Frontal passages are objective candidates based on three-hour pressure, temperature, wind and precipitation changes. A pressure, precipitation or strong-gust anchor is required to suppress ordinary diurnal temperature and wind cycles. The detector identifies local passage signatures; it does not replace a manually analysed synoptic front. Phenomena are deterministic candidates based on explicit thresholds; they are not manually quality-controlled reports. Observed station evidence is preferred, with gridded or model-derived evidence identified when observations are unavailable. Analogs are selected from 15 years of ERA5 daily data within +/-45 calendar days. Similarity uses standardized temperature, precipitation, wind, radiation, cloud and pressure; it is descriptive rather than predictive. Synoptic fields are model analyses from Open-Meteo Historical Forecast data. Frames are sampled every 6 hours on a 1-degree Central European grid. Vorticity, thermal advection and kinematic frontogenesis are finite-difference diagnostics derived on the reporting grid. A true 2-PVU dynamical-tropopause surface is not exposed by the no-secret provider and is not approximated. Standard anomalies use 30 same-calendar ERA5 periods from 1991-2020. Full-record percentiles use 36 same-calendar periods from 1990-2025. The recent-climate comparison uses 10 periods and remains separate from the WMO standard-normal window. Rolling soil, VPD and ET0 fields use Open-Meteo Historical Weather best-match gridded data, not station measurements. The 1991-2020 water-balance reference is fixed to ERA5; the rolling best-match series can use newer IFS and ERA5/ERA5-Land inputs. Water balance is precipitation minus FAO-56 reference evapotranspiration and does not include runoff or irrigation. Dry/wet context uses the 1991-2020 distribution of same-calendar water-balance windows. PV yield models a south-facing 35-degree fixed array per installed kWp using plane-of-array irradiance and cell-temperature derating. Wind output uses observed/modelled 100 m wind, moist-air density correction, and a generic 3/12/25 m/s cut-in/rated/cut-out power curve. These are reference-system weather yields, not metered production or a forecast. Observational Coverage How much of the reporting window each observational input actually covers, by local day. A day below its threshold is marked. pages.title: Atlas
pages.visible_text: Debrecen meteorological record Atlas What kind of weather did Debrecen just have, how unusual was it, and what did it imply for solar and wind energy potential? Atlas is a deterministic weather diary for Debrecen. It combines airport observations, remote sensing, gridded climate records, atmospheric diagnostics, historical analogs and physically based renewable-energy estimates in two regularly updated publications. Current publications Daily public Daily Public Report The last complete local day, with a concise weather account, objective events, renewable yield and climate context. Latest edition 2026-10-27 → 72-hour expert Meteorological Analysis Surface, synoptic, satellite, radar, upper-air, land-surface, climate and energy diagnostics for the latest complete period. Current window 2026-10-25 to 2026-10-27 → Preserved record Report Archive One search across saved reports, rolling analyses and their de-duplicated objective weather-event evidence. Browse history Open archive → Evidence, not decoration The report begins with what was observed and labels every gridded, remotely sensed or model-derived contribution. Interactive figures support inspection, while deterministic text records the thresholds and evidence behind each interpretation. Observed HungaroMet Debrecen Airport Remote-sensed Radar + LINET + Meteosat Model-derived Open-Meteo + ERA5 Derived Column diagnostics + renewable yield Geographic scope Debrecen, Hungary Climate reference 1991-2020 standard normal, recent decade and full record Publication cadence Daily public record and rolling 72-hour analysis Scientific frame Atlas is descriptive, diagnostic, climatological and energy-oriented. It is not forecast calibration, an operational warning service or a plant-level production forecast. Open data The pipeline uses public HungaroMet, Open-Meteo and Energy-Charts endpoints without repository secrets. Optional-source failures remain explicitly unavailable rather than becoming false zeroes. Project notes Methods, source provenance and implementation details are maintained in the Atlas repository . Every analytical page includes its own evidence notes and machine-readable downloads.

pages.title: About | Atlas
pages.visible_text: Record type Daily observation Observed, not forecast Observed period 2026-10-27 Integrity Complete Required observation coverage passed Updated 2026-10-28 17:17 UTC Debrecen, Hungary - 2026-10-27 About This Report What is observed, what is model-derived, and when the daily publication updates. Publication The public report is rebuilt daily from the last complete Europe/Budapest calendar day. It uses the same deterministic calculations as the meteorological analysis, with shorter explanations and fewer diagnostics. Evidence HungaroMet station, radar, LINET and Meteosat products are observational or remotely sensed. Open-Meteo supplies continuous gridded surface fields, model pressure levels and ERA5 climate fields. Optional-source failures are reported as unavailable, never treated as observed zeroes. Climate references "Normal" means the 1991-2020 ERA5 standard reference. The recent-decade comparison and full-record percentile are shown separately.
